samples.q:
Cash rises by €1,000 after a bank loan.
How much profit does the loan create?
samples.answer:
A loan increases cash and debt equally.
It does not create revenue or profit.
samples.title: Edlintics Quiz 01 — Cash is not profit
samples.verification: Assets +1000; liabilities +1000; equity and profit unchanged. Ignore interest and fees.
samples.caption: Cash arrives. Has profit arrived too? A business borrows €1,000 from a bank, with no interest or fees to consider. A: profit rises €1,000. B: no change. C: profit falls €1,000. Choose before swiping, then explain your reasoning. #Accounting #LearnAccounting #Edlintics

samples.q:
An investment rises 20%, then falls 20%.
What is your €100 worth now?
samples.answer:
The 20% fall applies to €120, not €100.
The same percentage can mean a different amount.
samples.title: Edlintics Quiz 02 — Up 20%, down 20%
samples.concept: Successive percentage changes use different bases
samples.caption: Up 20%, then down 20%. What is your €100 investment worth now? A: €96. B: €100. C: €104. Assume no deposits, withdrawals or fees. Choose before swiping. Which amount is the second percentage applied to? #Finance #Percentages #Edlintics

samples.q:
Who has the comparative advantage
in making tables?
samples.answer:
Count the chairs sacrificed per table.
Being faster at everything is not the deciding factor.
samples.title: Edlintics Quiz 03 — Who should make the tables
samples.concept: Comparative advantage is lower opportunity cost
samples.verification: Maya gives up 8/4 = 2 chairs per table; Leo gives up 3/3 = 1 chair. Assume constant production trade-offs.
samples.caption: Maya can make 4 tables or 8 chairs in one day. Leo can make 3 tables or 3 chairs. Assume constant production trade-offs. Who has the comparative advantage in tables? A: Maya. B: Leo. C: same cost. Choose before swiping. Count what each person gives up. #Economics #OpportunityCost #Edlintics

samples.q:
The group means are 60 and 80.
What is the mean for all 40 students?
samples.answer:
Count students, not groups.
A larger group contributes more to the overall mean.
samples.title: Edlintics Quiz 04 — The average of averages
samples.concept: Combined means must be weighted by group size
samples.verification: (10 × 60 + 30 × 80)/(10 + 30) = 75. Each student has one equally weighted score on the same test.
samples.caption: 10 students average 60. Another 30 average 80 on the same test. What is the mean score for all 40 students? A: 70. B: 75. C: 80. Choose before swiping. Each student counts equally; the groups are different sizes. #Statistics #WeightedAverage #Edlintics
